thread:
maya: Heads up — customer 'Litmus' opened a ticket about MosaicX-v1 onboarding. p99 latency for long-context (6–8k tokens) requests jumped after yesterday's tokenizer swap. Seen across both hosted and dedicated routes.

rachel: Customer is seeing timeouts in their UI, error rate up ~4% on generate calls. They attached a curl repro and a trace.

maya: Quick repro we ran locally:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"mosaicx-v1","input":"<~7500-token prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
```

ash: Seen it in infra metrics too. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~300ms, p99 up ~1.6s. KV cache hit-rate drops on those requests, and tokenization cpu spike correlates with the window when tokenizer v0.7 was rolled.

liam: Initial hypothesis: the new BPE merge table changed split boundaries causing ~10% more sub-tokens for long inputs, which increases decoding time + KV cache pressure. Also noticed GC churn on the tokenizer process.

maya: Attaching a snippet from logs:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:31Z] request_id=r8f2 model=mosaicx-v1 seq_len=8192 tokens_out=256 tokenizer_time_ms=320 kernel_infer_ms=1150 kv_cache_misses=0.37 total_ms=1870
[2026-03-15T14:12:32Z] request_id=r8f3 model=mosaicx-legacy seq_len=8192 tokenizer_time_ms=90 kernel_infer_ms=1100 kv_cache_misses=0.05 total_ms=1240
```

rachel: Customer would prefer a fast workaround rather than waiting for a tokenizer patch. Any mitigation we can push from our side?

ash: Short-term options: 1) route long-context traffic to mosaicx-legacy (fallback) via rollout policy; 2) enable prefix KV caching for that tenant with longer TTL; 3) throttle batch sizes for long requests to avoid queueing. I can flip a canary route if we agree.

liam: Also recommend pinning tokenizer to v0.6 for MosaicX-v1 while we debug v0.7. The encode-time delta suggests extra sub-token expansion. I'll run a diff of token counts across a corpus.

maya: Can we do a quick rollback on the tokenizer variant for hosted users while we investigate?

ash: I can do a targeted rollback for the model pair today. Plan: set routing rule for tenant Litmus + any requests with seq_len>4000 -> mosaicx-legacy for 1hr, monitor p99. Deploy-bot will record change.

deploy-bot: Routing update scheduled by ash. Rule: seq_len>4000 route->mosaicx-legacy for tenants=[litmus] starting 2026-03-15T15:07:00Z. Change id: R-20260315-322.

maya: Thanks. I'll let the customer know and ask for a sample corpus to send to liam.

liam: Quick analysis result: average token inflation ~12% on long docs, and a small number of pathological unicode sequences (CJK + emoji clusters) that blow up BPE merges. Will produce a patch to normalization + merge table tomorrow.

rachel: Perfect. Customer is OK with a temporary routing fix. Can we also add a billing credit for the timeouts?

maya: I'll propose a 10% credit for the affected window and confirm with finance.

ash: Monitoring plan: watch p99 for mosaicx-legacy and mosaicx-v1, kv-cache hit-rate, tokenizer cpu. If rollback stabilizes p99 within 10 minutes, we'll keep the routing until liam's patch is validated.

liam: Repro steps for devs: run tokenizer count diff script on a random 500 long-docs set:
```
python tools/tokenizer_diff.py --model mosaicx-v1 --old-tokenizer v0.6 --new-tokenizer v0.7 --min-tokens 2000 --out=diffs.csv
```

maya: Leaving this in your hands. Tagging @ash for rollback and @liam for patch. I'll update the ticket and post timeline to the customer. :thumbsup:

ash: Done — route applied. Patch branch created: fix/tokenizer-normalize-mosaicx. I'll add canary metrics to the dashboard.

liam: Got a few failing sequences from the customer. Will PR tomorrow morning.

maya: Closing loop once PR lands and we validate on canary. Thanks everyone. :heart:
